fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire and emergency apparatus to reach the front entry without obstruction.
• Install a reflective address marker at the road edge so responders can identify the property at night or in low visibility.
• Trim any shrubs or plantings in the landscaped areas that narrow the driveway or block sightlines to the front entry.
• Mark or clearly identify any rear access points so responders are not limited to the single front approach when navigating to additional structures.
• Keep walkways between structures clear of stored items, equipment, or overgrown plantings so responders can move quickly on foot between buildings.
• Identify a flat, stable area near the driveway that emergency vehicles can use for staging without blocking the primary access route.
• Post visible signage or markers indicating the location of additional structures that are not directly visible from the front driveway.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin scattered shrubs around the property to create wider open gaps between individual plants.
• Remove any shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed or cut short in areas immediately surrounding the structure.
• Clear shrubs and low branches along the single access route so the driveway remains passable for emergency vehicles.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape areas immediately around the structure in a healthy, trimmed condition and remove any dead plant material promptly.
• Separate any shrub groupings that have grown together into continuous patches by thinning plants within those clusters.
